Merge data

data_eucs <- 
                list(
                    euc_saligna_residual_conductance_data,
                    euc_grandis_residual_conductance_data,
                    euc_crebra_residual_conductance_data,
                    euc_dunnii_residual_conductance_data,
                    euc_tereticornis_residual_conductance_data,
                    euc_melliodora_residual_conductance_data,
                    euc_sideroxylum_residual_conductance_data,
                    euc_fibrosa_residual_conductance_data) %>%
            
    reduce(rbind) %>% 
    
    mutate(
           # Log transform data for reducing variability
           gres = gres_mols_m2_s,
           dehydration_rate = transpiration_double_H2Ommol_per_sec_m2,
           temperature = as.numeric(set_temperature),
           
           # Create Fast vrs Slow groups
           group = factor(if_else(spcode == "euc_saligna" | spcode == "euc_grandis" | 
                          spcode == "euc_tereticornis" | spcode == "euc_dunnii", 
                          "fast", "slow")),
           
           # Rename levels in treatment
           treatment = factor(if_else(vpd_control == "no", "dry_heat", "humid_heat")),
           
           # Convert variables
           tree_id = factor(tree_id),
           spcode = factor(spcode),
           .keep = 'unused') %>% 
    
    # Sort columns
    dplyr::select(tree_id, spcode, group, treatment, temperature,  everything()) 
data_eucs_gres <- 
                list(
                    euc_saligna_residual_conductance_data,
                    euc_grandis_residual_conductance_data,
                    euc_crebra_residual_conductance_data,
                    euc_dunnii_residual_conductance_data,
                    euc_tereticornis_residual_conductance_data,
                    euc_melliodora_residual_conductance_data,
                    euc_sideroxylum_residual_conductance_data,
                    euc_fibrosa_residual_conductance_data
              ) %>%
            
    reduce(rbind) %>% 
    
    mutate(
           # Log transform data for reducing variability
           gres = gres_mols_m2_s,
           dehydration_rate = transpiration_double_H2Ommol_per_sec_m2,
           temperature = as.numeric(set_temperature),
           
           # Create Fast vrs Slow groups
           group = factor(if_else(spcode == "euc_saligna" | spcode == "euc_grandis" | 
                          spcode == "euc_tereticornis" | spcode == "euc_dunnii", 
                          "fast", "slow")),
           
           # Rename levels in treatment
           treatment = factor(if_else(vpd_control == "no", "dry_heat", "humid_heat")),
           
           # Convert variables
           tree_id = factor(tree_id),
           spcode = factor(spcode),
           .keep = 'unused') %>% 
    
    # Remove 55C
    filter(!(temperature == 55)) %>%

    # Sort columns
    dplyr::select(tree_id, spcode, group, treatment, temperature,  everything()) %>% 
    
    # Remove unused variables
    dplyr::select(-c(branch_dry_matter_content_g_g, sla, branch_sla, lma, 
                     dehydration_rate))

Q1.1: What is the net effect of vpd over residual conductance?

Model fits

Linear model

model_gres_net_vpd_effect_linear <- glmmTMB(
    
                                            # Fixed effects
                                            log(gres) ~ treatment * poly(temperature, 1) +
                                                
                                            # Random intercepts and slopes
                                            (1 | spcode) + (1 + treatment | spcode:tree_id),
                                    data = data_eucs_gres,
                                    REML = TRUE
                                    )

Quadratic model

model_gres_net_vpd_effect_poly_1 <- update(model_gres_net_vpd_effect_linear, 
                                         
                                         # Fixed effects
                                         log(gres) ~ treatment * poly(temperature, 2) +
                                         
                                         # Random intercepts and slopes   
                                         (1 | spcode) + (1 + treatment | spcode:tree_id))

Model comparison linear vrs quadratic fit

anova(update(model_gres_net_vpd_effect_linear, REML = FALSE),
      update(model_gres_net_vpd_effect_poly_1, REML = FALSE)) %>% 
        
    as.data.frame() %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column("Model") %>%
    mutate(Model = c("Linear", "Quadratic"),
           `Pr(>Chisq)` = ifelse(`Pr(>Chisq)` < 0.001, "<0.001", 
                                 sprintf("%.3f", `Pr(>Chisq)`))) %>%
    
    knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Likelihood-ratio test: linear vs quadratic temperature response")
Likelihood-ratio test: linear vs quadratic temperature response
Model Df AIC BIC logLik deviance Chisq Chi Df Pr(>Chisq)
Linear 9 897.24 937.75 -439.62 879.24
Quadratic 11 812.78 862.29 -395.39 790.78 88.47 2 <0.001

Quadratic model + species linear temperature response with constant-variance

model_gres_net_vpd_effect_poly_2 <- glmmTMB(
        
                                        # Fixed effects
                                        log(gres) ~ treatment * poly(temperature, 2)  + 
    
                                        # Random intercepts and slopes, tree 
                                        # level responses to treatments
                                        (1 + treatment | spcode:tree_id) +
            
                                        # Species-level temperature responses    
                                        (1 + poly(temperature, 1) | spcode),
                                    
                                    data = data_eucs_gres,
                                    REML = TRUE)

Quadratic model + species quadratic temperature response with constant-variance

model_gres_net_vpd_effect_poly_3 <- glmmTMB(
        
                            # Fixed effects
                            log(gres) ~ treatment * poly(temperature, 2)  + 
                        
                            # Random intercepts and slopes, tree level 
                            # responses to treatments
                            (1 + treatment | spcode:tree_id) +
                                
                            # Species-level temperature responses    
                            (1 + poly(temperature, 2) | spcode),
                        
                        data = data_eucs_gres, 
                        REML = TRUE)

Check homogeneity of variances

cells <- interaction(data_eucs_gres$treatment, 
                     factor(data_eucs_gres$temperature))

car::leveneTest(residuals(model_gres_net_vpd_effect_poly_3, 
                          type = "pearson"), cells)
Levene's Test for Homogeneity of Variance (center = median)
       Df F value       Pr(>F)    
group  11  4.8963 0.0000002605 ***
      654                         
---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
residuals <- residuals(model_gres_net_vpd_effect_poly_3, type = "response")

residuals_standard_deviation <- predict(model_gres_net_vpd_effect_poly_3, type = "disp")  

# Under homogeneity of variance the ratio should be the same across every cell 
ratio_r_rsd <- residuals / residuals_standard_deviation
# Test if the ratio is the same across every cell 
car::leveneTest(ratio_r_rsd, cells)
Levene's Test for Homogeneity of Variance (center = median)
       Df F value       Pr(>F)    
group  11  4.8963 0.0000002605 ***
      654                         
---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

Quadratic model + species quadratic temperature response with variance modeled

model_gres_net_vpd_effect_poly_4 <- glmmTMB(
        
                            # Fixed effects
                            log(gres) ~ treatment * poly(temperature, 2)  + 
                        
                            # Random intercepts and slopes, tree level 
                            # responses to treatments
                            (1 + treatment | spcode:tree_id) +
                                
                            # Species-level temperature responses    
                            (1 + poly(temperature, 2) | spcode),
                            
                            # No constant variance 
                            dispformula = ~ treatment * poly(temperature, 2),
                            
                        data = data_eucs_gres, 
                        REML = TRUE)
residuals <- residuals(model_gres_net_vpd_effect_poly_4, type = "response")

 
residuals_standard_deviation <- predict(model_gres_net_vpd_effect_poly_4, type = "disp")  

ratio_r_rsd <- residuals / residuals_standard_deviation
car::leveneTest(ratio_r_rsd, cells)

       Df F value Pr(>F)
group  11  0.6644 0.7728
      654               
anova(
      model_gres_net_vpd_effect_poly_1,
      model_gres_net_vpd_effect_poly_2,
      model_gres_net_vpd_effect_poly_3,
      model_gres_net_vpd_effect_poly_4) %>% 
    
    as.data.frame() %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column("Model") %>%

                   "+ species linear slopes",
                   "+ species curvature",

           p = ifelse(is.na(`Pr(>Chisq)`), "",

    select(Model, Df, AIC, logLik, Chisq, `Chi Df`, p) %>%
    knitr::kable(digits = 1,
                 col.names = c("Model", "Df", "AIC", "logLik", "Chisq", "test df", "p"),
                 caption = "Model ladder for residual conductance (LRTs against the preceding model)") %>%
    kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)

Q2.1: Residual Conductance Fast vrs Slow responses

Model Fits

Linear model

model_gres_group_responses_linear <- glmmTMB(
    
            log(gres) ~ treatment * poly(temperature, 1) * group+

            # Random intercepts and slopes, tree level responses to treatments
            (1 | spcode) + (1 + treatment | spcode:tree_id),
       
      data = data_eucs_gres, 
      REML = TRUE)
diagnose(model_gres_group_responses_linear)
Unusually large coefficients (|x|>10):

theta_1+treatment|spcode:tree_id.3 
                         -236.8704 

Large negative coefficients in zi (log-odds of zero-inflation),
dispersion, or random effects (log-standard deviations) suggest
unnecessary components (converging to zero on the constrained scale);
large negative and/or positive components in binomial or Poisson
conditional parameters suggest (quasi-)complete separation. Large
values of nbinom2 dispersion suggest that you should use a Poisson
model instead.


Unusually large Z-statistics (|x|>5):

                     d~(Intercept) theta_1+treatment|spcode:tree_id.1 
                        -29.397192                          -8.689142 

Large Z-statistics (estimate/std err) suggest a *possible* failure of
the Wald approximation - often also associated with parameters that are
at or near the edge of their range (e.g. random-effects standard
deviations approaching 0).  (Alternately, they may simply represent
very well-estimated parameters; intercepts of non-centered models may
fall in this category.) While the Wald p-values and standard errors
listed in summary() may be unreliable, profile confidence intervals
(see ?confint.glmmTMB) and likelihood ratio test p-values derived by
comparing models (e.g. ?drop1) are probably still OK.  (Note that the
LRT is conservative when the null value is on the boundary, e.g. a
variance or zero-inflation value of 0 (Self and Liang 1987; Stram and
Lee 1994; Goldman and Whelan 2000); in simple cases these p-values are
approximately twice as large as they should be.)
VarCorr(model_gres_group_responses_linear)

Conditional model:
 Groups         Name                Std.Dev. Corr   
 spcode         (Intercept)         0.23535         
 spcode:tree_id (Intercept)         0.29499         
                treatmenthumid_heat 0.06323  -1.000 
 Residual                           0.42888         
performance::check_singularity(model_gres_group_responses_linear)

model_gres_group_responses_linear_2 <- glmmTMB(
    
    log(gres) ~ treatment * poly(temperature, 1) * group +
        
         # correlation parameter removed
        (1 | spcode) + diag(1 + treatment | spcode:tree_id),  
           
  data = data_eucs_gres,
  REML = TRUE)

Quadratic model

                            log(gres) ~ treatment * poly(temperature, 2) * group +
            
            # Random intercepts and slopes, tree level responses to treatments
            (1 | spcode) + (1 + treatment | spcode:tree_id),
            
            data = data_eucs_gres,
            REML = TRUE)

Quadratic model + species linear temperature response with constant-variance

model_gres_group_responses_poly_2 <- glmmTMB(
    
            log(gres) ~ treatment * poly(temperature, 2) * group +
             
            # Random intercepts and slopes, tree level responses to treatments
            (1 + treatment | spcode:tree_id) +
         
            # Species-level temperature responses e
            (1 + poly(temperature, 1) | spcode), 
                                    
      data = data_eucs_gres, 
      REML = TRUE)

Quadratic model + species quadratic temperature response with constant-variance

model_gres_group_responses_poly_3_1 <- glmmTMB(
    
            log(gres) ~ treatment * poly(temperature, 2) * group +
             
                    # Random intercepts and slopes, tree level responses 
                    # to treatments
                    (1 + treatment | spcode:tree_id) +
         
                    # Species-level temperature responses e
                    (1 + poly(temperature, 2) | spcode), 
         
      data = data_eucs_gres, 
      REML = TRUE)
model_gres_group_responses_poly_3_2 <- glmmTMB(
    
            log(gres) ~ treatment * poly(temperature, 2) * group +
             
                    # Random intercepts and slopes, tree level responses 
                    # to treatments
                    (1 + treatment | spcode:tree_id) +
         
                    # Species-level temperature responses e
                    diag(1 + poly(temperature, 2) | spcode), 
         
      data = data_eucs_gres, 
      REML = TRUE)

Model comparison

Check homogeneity of variances

cells <- interaction(data_eucs_gres$treatment, 
                     factor(data_eucs_gres$temperature))

car::leveneTest(residuals(model_gres_group_responses_poly_3_2, type = "pearson"), 
                cells)
Levene's Test for Homogeneity of Variance (center = median)
       Df F value         Pr(>F)    
group  11  5.8732 0.000000003883 ***
      654                           
---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
residuals <- residuals(model_gres_group_responses_poly_3_2, type = "response")

residuals_standard_deviation <- predict(model_gres_group_responses_poly_3_2, 
                                        type = "disp")  

# Under homogeneity of variace the ratio should be the same across every cell 
ratio_r_rsd <- residuals / residuals_standard_deviation
# Test if the ratio is the same across every cell 
car::leveneTest(ratio_r_rsd, cells)
Levene's Test for Homogeneity of Variance (center = median)
       Df F value         Pr(>F)    
group  11  5.8732 0.000000003883 ***
      654                           
---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

Quadratic model + species quadratic temperature response with variance modeled

model_gres_group_responses_poly_4 <- glmmTMB(
        
                            # Fixed effects
                            log(gres) ~ treatment * poly(temperature, 2) * group + 
                        
                            # Random intercepts and slopes, tree level 
                            # responses to treatments
                            (1 + treatment | spcode:tree_id) +
                                
                            # Species-level temperature responses    
                            (1 + poly(temperature, 2) | spcode),
                            
                            # No constant variance 
                            dispformula = ~ treatment * poly(temperature, 2),
                            
                        data = data_eucs_gres, 
                        REML = TRUE)
residuals <- residuals(model_gres_group_responses_poly_4, type = "response")

residuals_standard_deviation <- predict(model_gres_group_responses_poly_4, type = "disp")  

ratio_r_rsd <- residuals / residuals_standard_deviation
car::leveneTest(ratio_r_rsd, cells)
Levene's Test for Homogeneity of Variance (center = median)
       Df F value Pr(>F)
group  11  0.8782 0.5616
      654               
anova(model_gres_group_responses_poly_1,
      model_gres_group_responses_poly_2,
      model_gres_group_responses_poly_3_2,
      model_gres_group_responses_poly_4) %>% 

    as.data.frame() %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column("Model") %>%
    mutate(Model = c("+ Base (species intercepts)",
                   "+ species linear slopes",
                   "+ species curvature",
                   "+ dispersion submodel"),
           p = ifelse(is.na(`Pr(>Chisq)`), "",
                      ifelse(`Pr(>Chisq)` < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", `Pr(>Chisq)`)))) %>%
    select(Model, Df, AIC, logLik, Chisq, `Chi Df`, p) %>%
    knitr::kable(digits = 1,
                 col.names = c("Model", "Df", "AIC", "logLik", "Chisq", "test df", "p"),
                 caption = "Model ladder for residual conductance (LRTs against the preceding model)") %>%
    kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
